candidates.title: A comparison puts two runs' values of one name in different units on one row and reckons the change across the units
candidates.statement: A comparison row takes the first run's unit for every run's value of that name, whatever unit each run's outputs.values states, and computes each run's relative change across the two units, so the same titre written in g L-1 and in mg L-1 reads as a change of +99,900 %.
candidates.contract: docs/api/studies.md:140: "`rows` | `[{key, unit, values, change}]`: every output any run answers, each run's value (null for a run with no output of that key), and its relative change from the first run's ... a run of any other engine's are its outputs.values (`values.<name>`, each in its unit; `docs/api/runs.md`, Outputs)"
candidates.reproCommand: bash bughunt/notes/H2/scripts/repro_fresh.sh  (section H2-01; make_fit.py writes the two fits)
candidates.expected: Values of one name in two units kept apart (a row per unit) or held to one unit before the change is reckoned: the same product titre forecast from the same readings in g L-1 and in mg L-1 shows a change of 0.
candidates.observed: Row values.finals.product, unit 'g L-1', values [19.5338, 19533.85], change [0.0, 998.9998]; GET /api/runs/{second} states finals.product 19533.85 mg L-1. study_compare cites the change as evidence <comparison>:values.finals.product:2 = 998.9998 with unit 'fraction', and the export's study.md prints it as +99899.98 %.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/studies/comparisons.py:125-137 (`_rows`: `unit = next((u for u in units if u is not None), None)`; `_change` over the raw values with no unit check)
candidates.evidence: Two POST /api/fermos/fit of one logistic run, the product series in g L-1 and in mg L-1 (x1000), each forecast through POST /api/fermos/forecast; POST /api/studies/comparisons over the two forecast runs answered the row above; the same through the study_compare tool; reproduced on a fresh database (bh_h2_fresh, port 8823). Any two runs whose engine states a shared output name in two units meet the same row (a contract engine's outputs, a forecast's series units).

candidates.title: A Proforma scenario run replays outside the exact precision the biosteam engine states for it once the worker restarts
candidates.statement: A kept proforma.run artifact of ethanol_glucose_v0 replays identically in the worker that computed it and, after the service restarts, with one-ulp differences in nine TEA and utility numbers, so the replay answers identical false and withinTolerance false against the rtol 0, atol 0 the engine states for the flowsheet.
candidates.contract: docs/api/engines.md:616-618: "A scenario flowsheet's is `rtol` 0, `atol` 0: `proforma.run` registers no tolerance, so its replay holds every output identically." and docs/api/runs.md:229-231: "A Proforma run registers no tolerance either: its replay is `identical` or names its differences, and the biosteam engine's scenario flowsheets state rtol 0, atol 0."
candidates.expected: The run replays identically in any worker at the precision the thing states, as a library run's replay holds at the ten digits it keeps; or the thing states the precision its numbers keep.
candidates.observed: Replay in the worker that ran it: identical True. After bh_svc_stop and bh_svc_start over the same database: identical False, withinTolerance False, tolerance None, 9 differences (tea.FCI 21777995.078954738 -> 21777995.078954734, tea.TCI, tea.installedEquipmentCost, tea.lines[2].perUnit, tea.lines[2].usdPerYear, tea.purchaseCost, tea.utilityCost, utilities.electricityConsumption, utilities.heating). GET /api/engines states precision {rtol 0.0, atol 0.0} for ethanol_glucose_v0. nightly_checks.replay_newest counts such a replay a problem ('replays differently').
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/proforma.py:803-810 registers proforma.run with no tolerance_of and its output keeps every digit BioSTEAM gives (library.py:68-74 rounds a library run to DIGITS = 10 for this last-digit drift); proforma.py:1514-1523 states EnginePrecision(rtol=0.0, atol=0.0)
candidates.evidence: On bh_h2_main after a restart, be9d3a3b825fb83d (500 samples), 1a5a3b27a6d2e210 and de79b2992a6400e9 (20 samples) each replayed with the same nine differences, twice; the library runs, the vessel design, the train run, the composite custom_train_v1 run and the kinetics runs replayed identically in the same worker. Reproduced from a fresh database (bh_h2_rep, port 8822): identical before the restart, nine differences after.

candidates.title: A locked runbook's row keeps a lockedAt and lockHash other than its lock's, and the runbook then reads as a broken lock
candidates.statement: After a lock, PUT /api/state/runbooks/{id} with the frozen predictions and a rewritten lockedAt and lockHash is kept, and GET /api/studies/runbooks/{id} then answers that moment and digest in place of the ones runbook_locks keeps.
candidates.contract: docs/api/studies.md:170-174: "Locking freezes the predictions and measures under the digest the browser's own code writes ... with the moment: the lock is kept in `runbook_locks` and audited, then carried by the row." and docs/api/studies.md:184: "`GET /api/studies/runbooks/{id}` | Any runbook of the project, a lock the row does not carry laid on"
candidates.expected: The write refused in words, or the lock's own lockedAt and lockHash laid over the row's, once runbook_locks holds the lock.
candidates.observed: PUT with lockedAt 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z and lockHash 0000000000000000: 200. GET answers lockedAt 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z, lockHash 0000000000000000; the lock froze 2026-11-10T21:56:35Z under defaed1f2d69e44b. src/engine/lock.ts lockIntact compares the predictions' digest with the row's lockHash, so RunbookDetail shows 'lock broken' over predictions that are the frozen ones.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/project_state.py:579-584 (the store checks frozen_as over predictions and measures alone); core/openferment_core/studies/runbooks.py:67-71 (`_laid` lays the lock on only when the row carries no lockedAt)
candidates.evidence: lock_probe.py on bh_h2_main and on a fresh database: a moved prediction is refused 422 (held), the rewritten lock fields are kept 200 and served back; a row with the lock fields set null gets the lock laid back on.

candidates.title: A locked runbook is taken back whole through the state door, and made again it answers as an unlocked draft
candidates.statement: DELETE /api/state/runbooks/{id} removes a locked study runbook, its frozen predictions leaving GET, the listing and the export while its lock stays, and POST /api/studies/runbooks for the same run and outputs then answers lockedAt null and lockHash null although GET /api/studies/runbooks lists the same id locked.
candidates.contract: core/openferment_core/project_state.py:30-31: "What a person made, locked, measured or asked stays: a deposition, a measurement, a lock and a conversation are never taken back through here."; docs/api/studies.md:173-175: "From then on the store (`project_state.py`) refuses a runbook row whose predictions or measures are not the ones frozen, from the page or the service alike; its status and stages still move."
candidates.expected: A locked runbook refused at DELETE in words, as a deposition and a lock are; a make that finds the lock answering the runbook with it laid on.
candidates.observed: DELETE 200 {removed: true}; GET /api/studies/runbooks/rb-study-990b5b646ae3 404 'the project holds no runbook'; audit keep_runbooks, lock, remove_runbooks, keep_runbooks; POST /api/studies/runbooks again 200 with lockedAt None, lockHash None; GET /api/studies/runbooks lists rb-study-990b5b646ae3 with lockedAt 2026-11-10T21:56:35Z.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/project_state.py:144 (Kind('runbooks') stays removable whatever its lock); core/openferment_core/studies/runbooks.py:133-140 (make answers the Runbook it built, the lock not laid on)
candidates.evidence: lock_probe.py on bh_h2_main and on a fresh database. Whether a person may take back a locked runbook is the owner's rule to state; the answer of the make door disagreeing with the read door is shown either way.

candidates.title: The export package leaves out the kinetic fits its forecast runs rest on
candidates.statement: study.json carries each run's artifact and each comparison's and no artifact a kept basis names beyond those, so a forecast run's kinetic fit (its parameters and the readings it was fitted on) is absent from a package that is to open without the service.
candidates.contract: CLAUDE.md:8 (R): "every claim, number and result stays inspectable back to its source, its calculation and its assumptions"; docs/api/studies.md:234-236: "The project's studies as one zip that opens with nothing of openFerment's"
candidates.reproCommand: bash bughunt/notes/H2/scripts/repro_fresh.sh  (section H2-05; open_export.py runs under python3 -I -S)
candidates.expected: Every artifact a kept run's basis names (a forecast's fit, a Proforma run's chosen fit) inside study.json's artifacts, so each number traces to its source in the package alone.
candidates.observed: open_export.py: 'each artifact a kept artifact rests on held: MISSING' naming the two kinetic fits each growth_forecast run's basis names (input 'kinetic fit'). Every other check of the package held: manifest sizes and sha256, SFF files byte for byte, determinism between exports, the command line's package equal to the route's.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/studies/exports.py:97-102 (study(): the artifacts of the runs and of the comparisons alone)
candidates.evidence: Exports of h2a on bh_h2_main and of a fresh project; docs/api/studies.md:240 names 'the artifacts that computed the runs and the comparisons', which a fit is not, so the break is against the R line and the package's purpose.

candidates.statement: GET /api/library/oilcane/regression answers null, while GET /api/library/oilcane/parameters reads S1 and POST /api/library/oilcane/run {} runs in S1 held to test_oilcane_S1, 11 of 11.

candidates.contract: docs/api/studies.md:14: "`id` | `ssc-` and the first twelve hex of the sha256 of the plant, the configuration and the values: the same values on the same plant are one scenario"
candidates.expected: One scenario for the same values on the same plant in the same configuration, the configuration a run resolves to.
candidates.observed: ssc-dfb16a00b81f (no configuration) and ssc-a453c2dfc65c (S1) both run as 92285f57a6cc6c00, configuration S1, scenarioId ssc-dfb16a00b81f; the second scenario's runIds lists the run.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/studies/scenarios.py:148 hashes asked.configuration as made, while _checked (scenarios.py:105) and the run (engine/biosteam.py:188) resolve it to the default
